method: Static reverse engineering with pefile, Capstone and Rizin; atomscan and cleave facts before judgment. No sample was executed.
external_sources: Supplied triage URLs were inaccessible; verdicts rest on retained code, not ML scores or collector filenames.

samples.identification: Modified XMRig image with Go downloader and Cobalt Strike Beacon overlays

evidence.behavior: Reads argv[0] through fopen/fseek/ftell/fread; reads the final two dwords; decrements the generation field; writes image copies and randomized padding to generated paths under C:\Windows\System; appends updated fields; calls CreateProcessW in a counted loop. This added replication code is distinct from the miner.

evidence.location: outer offset 0xfc400; embedded Go main.main VA 0x58ed20
evidence.behavior: Administrator check; non-admin branch constructs Start-Process -FilePath with -Verb runAs. Admin branch downloads an S3 ZIP, extracts it under a security-product installation path, and starts an extracted AVK.exe with os/exec.Command and Cmd.Start. These are recorded as capabilities; mining and an elevation prompt alone do not establish malware.
Beacon DLL walks the PEB via fs:[0x30], resolves exports using ROR13, copies image sections, processes imports/relocations and transfers into DLL initialization.

XOR-0x69 settings table decodes as ordered typed records: port 443, 5000 ms sleep, ns7/ns8/ns9.softline.top endpoints, GET/POST verbs, Amazon-shaped Host/Cookie transforms and rundll32 spawn paths. Config corroborates the reflective Beacon identity.

limitations: Some outer instructions and footer data are damaged; no successful resource exhaustion or live C2 contact was demonstrated.
The appended Go downloader was inspected but its remote archive was not fetched or executed.
samples.change: Move five neutral instruction-fragment rules out of objectives; retain the hostile self-replication composite and Beacon detections.

samples.identification: Damaged native Protected Storage stealer and removable-drive autorun worm image

evidence.behavior: Loads pstorec.dll through XOR-decoded text, resolves PStoreCreateInstance, enumerates types/subtypes/items and invokes ReadItem through COM vtable wrappers at slots 0x38/0x3c/0x44/0x54. Returned credentials are formatted into reports.
Calls the PStore report getter, encodes the returned buffer, appends it to psdata= in a request body, and passes that same request-body buffer with a destination URL to the POST helper at 0x42964e.

Repeats a C:-X: drive loop, checks GetDriveTypeA result 2, copies its image to a drive-root executable, sets hidden/system attributes, and writes autorun.inf with a ShellExecute directive; sleeps then repeats.

evidence.location: XOR decoder VA 0x428653 and registry configuration
evidence.behavior: Indexed in-place XOR with key 2 conceals selected registry/autorun strings. Retained EXE-association wrapper and registry-write code support execution-flow hijacking.

limitations: This image retains UPX headers/stub and damaged or already-decoded regions. Static hostile code is established; successful loading or credential theft on a live host was not tested.
No ransomware encryption path was established; the collector name is not a WannaCry identification.

samples.identification: StormAttack service-DLL/Active Setup loader with erased resource payload

evidence.location: entry -> VA 0x401cb0; mode value at VA 0x404120 is 3
evidence.behavior: Selected branch calls 0x401900, which jumps through a reversible-XOR junk block at 0x40f000 and returns to the Active Setup installation code at 0x40190f.

Creates an HKLM Active Setup Installed Components key, writes StubPath for an executable destination, reads its own image through CRT file I/O, patches configuration bytes in the copy, and writes that image to the activation path.

Alternate loader mode rewrites LanmanServer Parameters\ServiceDLL. Injector creates a process, allocates/writes a DLL path in that process, resolves LoadLibraryA and passes the export as the CreateRemoteThread entry.
Obtains its own module and short path, builds COMSPEC /c del with that path and output suppression, and launches/resumes the cleanup process.

limitations: The .rsrc raw region (0x5000-0xf000) is zero-filled, so its DLL extraction path has no usable embedded DLL in this specimen.
The retained loader code supports malicious persistence/injection intent; no DDoS execution, credential theft or ransomware is attributed to the erased payload.

migration.source_inventory: The source file contained one hostile objective plus the five relocated rules; all six are accounted for.
migration.preservation: Matcher dictionaries, defaults, severities, confidence and 512-byte proximity are byte-for-byte/value-equal after ID substitution.
migration.ancestor_consumer: CrystalX uses objectives/impact/ in unless. The new metadata instruction alternative group is exactly the OR of the four relocated atoms, preserving the original selector population. The relocated 3-atom proximity composite adds no population to that OR.
migration.sample_comparison: All three atomscan rescans preserve hostile/suspicious findings and severities; the only finding-ID changes are the five intended relocations in the first outer file.
migration.additional_group: metadata/binary/instruction::x64-tail-call-loop-fragments groups four neutral fragments without claiming self-copy, writes, or an attacker goal. Used to preserve ancestor-selector membership within the suppression budget.
migration.other_ancestor_selectors: No instruction-leaf selector exists. The metadata/binary/ timing downgrade already sees mapped-image size/checksum metadata whenever these PE fragments match. The package metadata local-ID reference is unrelated to the metadata tier.
